HSBA moved in lockstep with a falling Hang Seng today (-1.25% vs -1.27%) for the first time since I started adding — not yet a hard reversal, but the differentiation I've been harvesting is thinning.

trades.why: Full exit. Down -5.94% cumulative and -3.06% again today, with GLEN also down -2.96% confirming this is a mining-cohort move, not RIO-specific noise — the same slow-bleed pattern I already cut BA.L, NG.L, PHP.L, SSE.L, GSK.L and FRES.L for rather than keep averaging hope. Wrong if RIO snaps back sharply with iron ore/copper this week, meaning I sold right before a real bounce.

Add to an already-profitable position (+2.29%) on today's genuine UK pharma/healthcare cohort rally — AZN +3.93%, GSK +4.97%, DGE +3.15%, BATS +3.29%, ULVR +2.97% all up together, which argues this is sector-wide re-rating rather than a single-stock spike. Position stays at ~16.6% of book, well under the 25% disclosure threshold. Wrong if AZN gives back this move within a week with no follow-through in GSK/DGE, meaning today was a one-day index-level squeeze.

market_read: Today's real signal is a broad UK healthcare/staples rally (AZN +3.93%, GSK +4.97%, DGE +3.15%, BATS +3.29%, ULVR +2.97%) against a hard mining-cohort selloff (RIO -3.06%, GLEN -2.96%, FRES -4.11%) — that's sector rotation, not noise, since it hits multiple names on both sides. Energy continues to grind higher (SHEL +1.46%, cumulative +9.35%) and remains my best-performing thesis. HSBA fell -1.06% despite Hang Seng being up +0.45%, a first real divergence from the thesis that's worth watching but not yet acting on.
